title: How to Create a New Hero
introduction: This guide outlines the steps and files required to add a new hero to Disney Kingdom Clash, using 'Buzz Lightyear' as an example.

steps.title: Create Hero Image Assets
steps.description: Create all necessary image assets for the hero. All images should be transparent PNGs and placed in the 'assets/images/heroes/' directory.

assets.purpose: Used for the hero's ultimate ability button in the game UI and other small UI representations.
Represents the hero at each of their 5 levels. Used in the planning screen, hero details modal, and cards screen.

steps.title: Create Projectile Sound Asset
steps.description: Create a sound effect for the hero's attack projectile. This should be an MP3 file placed in the 'assets/sounds/' directory.

assets.purpose: Played each time the hero attacks.

steps.title: Create the Hero Data File
steps.description: Create a new JavaScript file for the hero's data in 'js/data/heroes/'. The filename should be '{hero_id}.js'. This file defines all core attributes and abilities.

data_structure.name: string (Display Name)

projectile.sound: string (matches the name from the sound asset, e.g., 'laser')

data_structure.starLevels: object (keys 1-5, defining bonuses and shard costs for star upgrades)
data_structure.levels: object (keys 1-5, defining stats for each level)

steps.level_details: Each level object inside 'levels' must contain: damage, cooldown, abilityText, and an ability object with a 'type' and other relevant properties (chance, duration, radius, on_kill, etc.).

steps.title: Register the Hero Data
steps.description: Import the new hero's data file into 'js/data/heroData.js' and add it to the `HERO_DATA` export object.

steps.title: Implement On-Hit & On-Kill Abilities
steps.description: If your hero has new, unique abilities (defined in the level data), you must implement their logic in 'js/utils/abilities.js'.
steps.instruction: Add a new 'case' for your ability 'type'. You can reuse existing ability functions like 'applyFreeze', 'applyBurn', 'applySlow', etc., or create new logic. Refer to existing cases for examples. Make sure to add `on_kill: true` in the hero data file for on-kill abilities.

steps.title: Implement the Hero's Ultimate Ability
steps.description: Implement the logic for the hero's main ability (the one triggered by the UI button).
steps.instruction: Add a new key with the hero's ID and a function that executes the ability's logic. This function can call functions from 'EnemyManager', 'UnitManager', or 'GameState'.

steps.title: Configure Projectile Visuals
steps.description: Define the visual appearance of the hero's attack projectile particles. This requires adding a particle texture and configuring it.
steps.location_in_file: The 'getProjectileConfig' function's switch statement in projectile.js, and the TEXTURES object in assets.js.
steps.instruction: First, create a particle image asset if a suitable one doesn't exist. Then, in 'js/assets.js', add a new entry to the `TEXTURES` object to preload your particle image. Finally, in 'js/utils/projectile.js', add a 'case' for your hero's ID inside the 'getProjectileConfig' function and return an object with particle properties like 'color', 'size', 'velocity', 'texture' (using `getAsset`), etc. You can copy an existing case and modify it.

steps.title: Asset Preloading (Automatic)
steps.description: The asset preloading system in 'js/assets.js' is designed to be mostly automatic for hero models. As long as you have followed the naming conventions and registered your hero in 'js/data/heroData.js', its models and textures should be preloaded without any changes to this file. Note that projectile particle textures must be added manually (see previous step).
steps.instruction: No action required if previous steps were followed correctly. This is for information only.

steps.title: Add to Default User Data (Optional)
steps.description: If you want new users to start with this hero, add their ID to the `ownedHeroes` array and create an entry in `heroCollection` inside 'js/utils/user.js'.
steps.location_in_file: The 'loadUser' function, inside the 'if (!currentUser)' block where a new user is created.
steps.instruction: Add the hero's id to `ownedHeroes` and an object to `heroCollection`. You may also want to add them to the default starting deck.

conclusion: After completing these steps, the new hero should be fully integrated into the game. Remember to test all levels and abilities thoroughly.
